stem: A pipeline populates reporting tables that the business reads each morning, and the platform team wants the compute released once the night's data is through. They are choosing between the two execution modes the pipeline offers.

option_texts.A: Triggered mode, which refreshes the data available at the start and then stops
option_texts.B: Continuous mode, which refreshes everything once and then releases its compute
option_texts.C: Triggered mode, which keeps the tables fresh as each new record arrives
option_texts.D: Continuous mode, which is the only mode that can be started on a schedule

drill_answer_short: Triggered mode refreshes the data available when the update started and then stops; continuous keeps tables fresh
decision_hinge: Triggered mode refreshes available data and stops, while continuous mode keeps tables fresh as new data arrives, and in triggered mode the system stops after refreshing all tables based on the data available when the update started.

plausible_options.B: wants the compute released once the night's data is through

eliminated_by.C: populates reporting tables that the business reads each morning
eliminated_by.D: choosing between the two execution modes the pipeline offers

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - the described behaviour is right but it belongs to the other mode
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - staying fresh per arrival is continuous, not triggered
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a triggered pipeline is the one normally run on a schedule

stem: A pipeline left running without stopping reads from several upstream Delta tables that change only a few times a day. Finance expects the bill to track the work actually done rather than the hours the pipeline is up.

option_texts.A: It recomputes on a fixed interval whatever the upstream tables have done
option_texts.B: It monitors the dependent tables and updates only when their contents have changed
option_texts.C: It recomputes continuously, so the bill does follow the hours rather than the work
option_texts.D: It pauses itself between upstream changes and has to be restarted by an operator

drill_answer_short: In continuous mode pipelines monitor dependent Delta tables and update only when their contents change
decision_hinge: To avoid unnecessary processing in continuous execution mode, pipelines automatically monitor dependent Delta tables and perform an update only when the contents of those dependent tables have changed.

plausible_options.C: Finance expects the bill to track the work actually done

eliminated_by.A: reads from several upstream Delta tables that change only a few times a day
eliminated_by.D: A pipeline left running without stopping

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - a fixed interval is how a scheduled refresh behaves, not continuous mode
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - the mode exists with dependency monitoring precisely to avoid that
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a continuous pipeline does not pause itself awaiting an operator

stem: A bug was found in a transformation that has been running for weeks, and the corrected logic must be applied to every record ever ingested, not just the ones arriving next. The team is weighing what the heavier refresh option actually does.

option_texts.A: It truncates the targets but leaves the checkpoints, so only new records are read
option_texts.B: It replays the recorded history of the target without returning to the source
option_texts.C: It clears the checkpoints from flows and reprocesses all records from the source
option_texts.D: It re-runs only the flows whose source code changed since the previous update

drill_answer_short: A full refresh clears checkpoints from flows and reprocesses all records from the data source
decision_hinge: A full refresh clears checkpoints from flows and reprocesses all records from the data source.

plausible_options.B: the corrected logic must be applied to every record ever ingested

eliminated_by.A: not just the ones arriving next
eliminated_by.D: A bug was found in a transformation that has been running for weeks

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - leaving the checkpoints is what makes an ordinary refresh incremental
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - replaying target history sounds complete but never revisits the source records
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - selecting changed flows is a scope choice, not a reprocessing one

stem: A query writes out far more small files than the team wants, and they would rather state the partition count in the statement than change a cluster-wide setting. They are looking for the hint that reduces the number of output partitions.

option_texts.A: A CACHE hint, which holds the result until the partition count settles
option_texts.B: A BROADCAST hint, which collapses the output onto one executor
option_texts.C: A SKEW hint, which rebalances the output into a smaller number of partitions
option_texts.D: A COALESCE hint, which asks for a specified number of partitions

drill_answer_short: COALESCE and REPARTITION are partitioning hints that set the number of output partitions for a statement
decision_hinge: The partitioning hints COALESCE, REPARTITION, and REPARTITION_BY_RANGE take a partition number and correspond to the coalesce, repartition, and repartitionByRange operations.

plausible_options.C: they would rather state the partition count in the statement

eliminated_by.A: the hint that reduces the number of output partitions
eliminated_by.B: writes out far more small files than the team wants

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - caching does not set an output partition count
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - a broadcast hint shapes a join, not the number of output partitions
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - skew handling rebalances work but is not a partition-count hint

stem: A stewardship team wants the rows that fail validation kept somewhere they can be inspected and corrected, while the clean rows carry on downstream. Dropping the bad rows outright would lose the evidence they need.

option_texts.A: Flag each row against the rules and route the flagged ones to a quarantine table
option_texts.B: Drop the bad rows and read the dropped count from the dataset metrics afterwards
option_texts.C: Fail the update on the first bad row, so the records stay in the source for review
option_texts.D: Warn only, so the bad rows land in the target mixed in with the clean ones

drill_answer_short: The quarantine pattern flags records against the rules and routes invalid ones to a separate table for inspection
decision_hinge: To quarantine invalid records you define quarantine rules and add an is_quarantined flag, then route those records to a separate quarantine table rather than dropping them.

plausible_options.B: wants the rows that fail validation kept somewhere they can be inspected

eliminated_by.C: while the clean rows carry on downstream
eliminated_by.D: Dropping the bad rows outright would lose the evidence they need

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - the count is recorded, but the rows themselves are gone
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated requirement - stopping the update halts the clean rows too
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - warning keeps the rows but mixes them into the clean output
